questions.text:
Assume that a 12-bit Hamming codeword consisting of 8-bit data and 4 check bits is [latex]d_8d_7d_6d_5c_8d_4d_4d_3d_2c_4d_1c_2c_1[/latex], where the data bits and the check bits are given in the following tables:

Which one of the following choices gives the correct values of x and y?
questions.solution:
Positions: 1 c1, 2 c2, 3 d1, 4 c4, 5 d2, 6 d3, 7 d4, 8 c8, 9 d5, 10 d6, 11 d7, 12 d8 (even parity).
- c1 checks d1, d2, d4, d5, d7 = 1 + 0 + 0 + x + 1 = x. Given c1 = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] x = 0.
- c8 checks d5, d6, d7, d8 = 0 + 0 + 1 + 1 = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] y = 0.
(c2 and c4 also match: 1 and 0.)

Answer: x is 0 and y is 0

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: x is 0 and y is 0
x is 0 and y is 1
x is 1 and y is 0
x is 1 and y is 1

questions.text:
Consider the following two statements.

S1: Destination MAC address of an ARP reply is a broadcast address.
S2: Destination MAC address of an ARP request is a broadcast address.

Which one of the following choices is correct?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- ARP request: the sender does not know the MAC, so it is broadcast [latex]\text{---}[/latex] S2 TRUE.
- ARP reply: sent directly (unicast) to the requester's MAC [latex]\text{---}[/latex] S1 FALSE.

Answer: S1 is false and S2 is true

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Both S1 and S2 are true
S1 is true and S2 is false
S1 is false and S2 is true
Both S1 and S2 are false

questions.text: Remote Procedure Calls are used for
questions.solution:
RPC lets a program call a procedure in another address space, usually on another machine, but it can also be used between processes on the same machine. Since no single option is complete, the key marks "none of the above".

(This question was excluded from ISRO's evaluation because of its unclear wording.)

Answer: none of the above

questions.text: Checksum field in TCP header is
questions.solution:
The TCP checksum is the one's complement of the one's complement sum of 16-bit words of the pseudo header + TCP header + data.

The key also accepts option 3: IPv6 dropped the header checksum and relies on TCP/UDP checksums, which is why the TCP checksum (with the pseudo header) is mandatory there.

Answer: Options 2 and 3

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: ones complement of sum of header and data in bytes
ones complement of sum of header, data and pseudo header in?16?bit words
dropped from IPv6 header format
better than md5 or sh1 methods

questions.text: The persist timer is used in TCP to
questions.solution:
If the receiver advertises a zero window and the later window-update segment is lost, both sides would wait forever. The persist timer makes the sender send window probes, which avoids this deadlock.

Answer: To avoid deadlock condition

To enable retransmission
To avoid deadlock condition
